request.deadline: 18 months, with listed milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Establish or host a not-for-profit entity under a preliminary board and publish a technical transition architecture and migration plan in Q3 2026.
Launch a public usage dashboard in Q3 2026.
Hold a board election via on-chain voting under publicly published rules in Q4 2026.
Serve all public API traffic for mainnet, preview, and preprod from the new stack in Q1 2027.
Legally transfer Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to the governing entity in Q1 2027.
Open a public sustainability consultation and publish a long-term model proposal in Q2-Q3 2027.
Operate the public API at a minimum 99% monthly uptime SLA during 2027 and publish quarterly technical and budget reports.
request.what: Fund an 18-month transition of Blockfrost into a free, community-governed not-for-profit public API for Cardano, including operations during the transition period.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is described as a reliable hosted REST interface that lets developers read from and interact with Cardano without running their own infrastructure or node.
The proposal states that Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem surveys report Blockfrost hosted-platform usage rising from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025.
The proposal states that last month Blockfrost served 781,000 unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data.
The proposal states that in most Cardano epochs more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost.
The proposer says 90% of all Cardano traffic served through the Blockfrost API comes from the free tier, making the commercial model difficult for financing the public-good operation.

The proposal commits that all Blockfrost intellectual property, including source code, trademarks, domains, and associated assets, will be transferred to the governing not-for-profit entity as part of the transition.
The proposed governance model uses a five-seat board, with four seats for open-source infrastructure development entities and one community seat, preceded by a named preliminary board.
The proposal requests 9,832,979 ADA, equal to 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, with 79.1% for staffing, 19.3% for operations and infrastructure, and 1.6% for legal and accounting.
The proposal states that unspent post-transition infrastructure budget will be returned to the treasury and that quarterly reports will include technical data and a budget summary.

The proposal says Intersect will administer treasury funds through 2026 Treasury Reserve and Project-Specific Smart Contracts, with an external Oversight Committee verifying key administrative actions using on-chain logic.

summary: The document requests 9,832,979 ADA to fund Blockfrost's 18-month conversion from a commercial service into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, citing high developer adoption, heavy free-tier usage, IP transfer, governance formation, service migration, public dashboards, quarterly reporting, and smart-contract-based treasury administration.
